data.description:
# The conference timezone is the only timezone

## The ruling (Atin, 2026-08-14)

> The conference time zone is the only time zone, and we should display what time zone if
> necessary, if relevant. But generally speaking, this is one event, this one event happens
> in one time zone, we use that time to schedule that event. It's a universal thing.

One event, one clock. Every time an organizer **sets** and every time a human **reads** is
conference-local. Neither the browser's zone nor the Worker's zone may ever decide what a
conference time means. Where the reader could reasonably be elsewhere, name the zone.

## What set this off, and the worse one underneath it

sbek round 11 (`eval:2026-08-14T14-46-26:call-for-papers:2`) filed the CFP close date: an
organizer typed `2027-04-30 23:59`, saved, and the field redisplayed `05/01/2027, 03:59`.
`datetime-local` carries no zone, so both ends must agree on one, and these disagreed —
`src/ui/forms/FormsPage.tsx:493` writes with `new Date(value).getTime()` (**browser-local**)
and reads with `toISOString().slice(0,16)` (**UTC**). The stored instant was right; the
read-back lied.

PR #244 fixed that control by making both ends browser-local. It is **closed**, superseded
by the ruling above — but its branch `mrq-eval11-closedate` is preserved and its test file
`tests/unit/forms-close-date.eval11.test.ts` is a working starting point: it already pins a
non-UTC zone and covers a DST round trip. Read the PR and the branch before starting.

**The same fault has a second instance that is strictly worse.**
`src/ui/submissions/SubmissionRecordPage.tsx:660` places a session on the agenda from a
`datetime-local` parsed as `new Date(schedule.starts_at).getTime()` — browser-local — while
*every* downstream reader of `sessions.starts_at` (agenda grid, portal, ICS, board, public
schedule) renders it in `events.timezone`. An organizer in London placing a talk at "09:00"
for a New York conference schedules it for **04:00**. That is not a read-back fault; the
wrong instant is stored, and the talk is genuinely at the wrong time. `AgendaPage` does this
correctly via `zonedStart`; this screen does not.

## What is already right — do not churn it

A large part of the codebase already does exactly what the ruling asks. Leave it alone and
copy its patterns:

| Already conference-zoned | Evidence |
|---|---|
| Agenda grid, day/time derivation | `src/ui/agenda/track-board.tsx:124` `localParts`, `src/ui/agenda/AgendaPage.tsx:92` `zonedStart` |
| ICS `DTSTART;TZID=` + `X-WR-TIMEZONE` | `src/jobs/calendar/ics.ts:99` `localDateTime`, `src/lib/public-ics.ts:21` |
| Speaker portal slot day/time/leave-by | `src/routes/portal.routes.ts` (3 `Intl` calls, `timeZone: event.timezone`), `src/ui/portal/PortalPage.tsx:247` |
| Board and record slot rendering | `src/api/board.ts:217`, `src/routes/submission-record.routes.ts:171,181` |
| Public schedule clock + starring | `src/ui/public/agenda/schedule-script.ts:84` |
| Conflict detection, venue geometry, file-export folder names | `src/lib/conference-dates.ts:36`, `src/lib/venue-geometry.ts:95`, `src/routes/files-export.routes.ts:87,225` |
| Round-close day key | `src/routes/evaluation.routes.ts:280` `localDayKey` |

`Intl.DateTimeFormat` with an explicit `timeZone` is therefore already **proven on
Cloudflare Workers** — `src/jobs/calendar/ics.ts` runs there and the ICS tests assert its
output. No new dependency is needed and none should be added: `package.json` carries no
date library (hono, preact, zod, aws4fetch only), and `zonedStart`/`localParts` are a
working DST-correct inverse pair already in the tree.

## The zone itself

- `events.timezone TEXT NOT NULL` — `migrations/0001_init.sql:21`. Never null.
- Validated as a real IANA zone on create and update: `assertTimezone`,
  `src/routes/event-settings.routes.ts:247`, called at `:458` and `:553`. A bad zone is a
  422, so an invalid value cannot reach a reader through the API.
- **Reachable from any shell screen with no plumbing**: `useEventContext().event.timezone`
  (`src/ui/shell/event-context.tsx:24,177`). `EventProvider` is mounted at `ShellEntry`
  (`src/ui/app.tsx:53,80`) precisely so it also reaches `/delivery-health`.
- `event` is `null` while the events list is loading. **Do not fall back to the browser's
  zone** — that reintroduces this bug intermittently and invisibly. Render the placeholder
  the surface already uses for absent values (`—`, or the reserved-space span) until the
  zone is known.
- Public surfaces already carry it: `PublicEvent.timezone` (`src/lib/public-site.ts:28`),
  so `PublicEmbedData.event.timezone` is in scope inside `EmbedPage`.
- **Not carried on the public form payload.** `PublicFormState.conference` is
  `{ name, slug }` only (`src/routes/public-form.types.ts:45`). The query that builds it
  already joins the events table (`src/routes/public-form.shared.ts:248`), so this is one
  extra selected column plumbed through `:287` and `:359`.

### A defect found on the way in

`src/ui/settings/EventSettings.tsx:269` offers **four** timezone options (New York, Los
Angeles, London, UTC) while `src/ui/setup/CreateConferencePage.tsx:27` offers **eight**
(adding Chicago, Denver, Berlin, Tokyo, Sydney). A conference created in `Asia/Tokyo` opens
its own settings and the select shows `America/New_York` — the screen states the wrong zone
for the conference. `CreateConferencePage:296` already handles this correctly with
`[...new Set([timezone, ...TIMEZONES])]`. Fix it the same way, from one shared list. In a
build where the conference zone becomes the only zone, the screen that reports it must not
be able to misreport it.

## Consumer inventory

**BEHAVIOUR** = changing it moves a stored instant, or moves when something fires.
**DISPLAY** = the stored instant is unchanged and only the rendering is wrong.

### BEHAVIOUR — a wrong instant gets stored or acted on

| # | Site | Today | Required |
|---|---|---|---|
| B1 | `src/ui/submissions/SubmissionRecordPage.tsx:660` | `new Date(value).getTime()` — browser-local → `sessions.starts_at` | Conference-zone wall clock → instant. Reuse the same conversion `AgendaPage.zonedStart` uses. |
| B2 | `src/ui/forms/FormsPage.tsx:493` (write half) | `new Date(value).getTime()` — browser-local → `forms.closes_at` | Conference-zone wall clock → instant. **This genuinely moves when the CFP closes and when the reminder fires** for any organizer outside the conference zone — by design, and it is the correction, not a regression. |
| B3 | `speaker_tasks.due_at` enforcement — `src/jobs/mail/schedule.ts:88` (`due_at < ?`) against storage from `src/lib/task-due.ts:19` (end of **UTC** day) | A task due "May 1" goes overdue at 23:59:59.999Z = **19:59 EDT on May 1** | A speaker gets their whole day in the conference zone. Either derive the enforcement boundary from the calendar day + `events.timezone` at query time (the query has `task.event_id`; it needs a `JOIN events`), or migrate storage. Prefer the former — it changes no stored row. |

The `forms.closes_at` gates themselves are **already correct and need no change** — every
one is a pure instant comparison, which is zone-free by construction:
`src/routes/public-form.shared.ts:234-239`, `src/lib/public-site.ts:980-981`,
`src/routes/forms.routes.ts:239,510`, `src/routes/portal.routes.ts:1121`,
`src/lib/delivery-health.ts:586`, and the reminder window at
`src/jobs/mail/schedule.ts:42-43`. Do not touch them. The only behaviour that moves is what
instant B2 writes.

### DISPLAY — the instant is right, the rendering is wrong

| # | Site | Today | Required |
|---|---|---|---|
| D1 | `src/ui/forms/FormsPage.tsx:493` (read half) | `toISOString().slice(0,16)` — UTC | Conference-zone wall clock, symmetric with B2. **This is the reported bug.** |
| D2 | `src/ui/public/form/PublicForm.tsx:652` | `new Date(closes_at).toLocaleDateString()` — browser-local | Conference zone. Needs the payload change above. |
| D3 | `src/ui/public/form/PublicForm.tsx:69` `closeLabel` | `Intl` with no `timeZone` — browser-local | Conference zone. Same payload. |
| D4 | `src/ui/embeds/EmbedPage.tsx:303` `formatDeadline`, called at `:414` via `cfpBody(:409)` | `Intl` with no `timeZone` | Conference zone. `data.event.timezone` is already in scope in `EmbedPage:427`; thread it through `cfpBody`. **This one is embedded on third-party sites — the reader is definitionally elsewhere, so it must carry a zone label.** |
| D5 | `src/jobs/mail/schedule.ts:68` | `"form.closes_at": new Date(...).toISOString()` | The mail body literally reads `2027-05-01T03:59:00.000Z` (template: `src/jobs/mail/templates.ts:50`, "The form closes on {{form.closes_at}}"). Render conference-local, human, zone-labelled. Query needs `events.timezone`. |
| D6 | `src/jobs/mail/schedule.ts:115` | `"task.due_date": ...toISOString()` | Same. |
| D7 | `src/jobs/mail/merge-data.ts:47-51` | `session.time` and `task.due_date` are raw ISO, while `session.leaveBy` at `:29-35` is already zone-aware | Make all three consistent. `RecipientMergeContext` already carries `timezone`. |
| D8 | `src/ui/settings/EventSettings.tsx:269` | Four-option select misreports the conference's own zone | One shared list, plus the current value unioned in. |

### Leave as-is — and say why in the ticket's own words

These render **system and audit** timestamps, not conference times: when a webhook fired,
when a token was last used, when a comment was posted, when a review was saved. The reader
is the person at the keyboard, and their own clock is the right one.

`src/ui/settings/WebhooksPage.tsx`, `src/ui/settings/ApiTokensPage.tsx`,
`src/ui/comms/CommsScreen.tsx:119`, `src/ui/health/DeliveryHealthPage.tsx:67,71`,
`src/ui/files/FileComments.tsx`, `src/ui/portal/FileComments.tsx`,
`src/ui/files/FileVersions.tsx`, `src/ui/files/FilesPage.tsx`,
`src/ui/speakers/SpeakerFilesPanel.tsx`, `src/ui/onboarding/OnboardingPage.tsx:83,88`,
`src/ui/submissions/record-copy.ts`, `src/ui/review/ReviewerPage.tsx:727,761`,
`src/ui/public/form/PublicForm.tsx:641` ("Saved 3:42 PM" — the submitter's own clock is
correct and a conference zone here would be noise), `src/ui/shell/error-reporting.ts`,
`src/lib/observability/log.ts`, `src/routes/telemetry.routes.ts`.

If a later reviewer disagrees about any single one of these, that is a conversation, not a
defect. What must not happen is a sweeping find-and-replace that drags audit timestamps
into the conference zone and makes "when did this webhook fire" unanswerable from the
operator's own desk.

## The UTC contract: it coexists, and here is why

`76eb02e7` (#233) — "CONTRACT · reviewer round close dates use UTC calendar days" — and
`MRQ-114` (`src/lib/task-due.ts`) both pin to UTC deliberately. **The ruling does not
overturn them, because they were never really about UTC.**

Read their own reasons: *"a due date the organizer types must be the due date they read
back"* (`tests/unit/task-due.MRQ-114.test.ts:1-7`) and *"a review round that opens a day
early is a wrong answer, not a rounding one"* (`src/ui/evaluation/EvaluationPage.tsx:29-33`).
Both chose **one agreed anchor instead of the reader's machine** — which is precisely what
the ruling demands. UTC was the mechanism; the intent is identical.

They stay because a **calendar day is not a timezone-bearing value.** "The round closes
May 1" is the same sentence in New York and Tokyo. These fields are `<input type="date">`
with no clock (`EvaluationPage.tsx:717-718`, `TaskTemplatesPage.tsx:311`); the ruling
governs *times*, and there is no time here for a zone to apply to. Two facts settle it:

1. **Nothing gates on evaluation round dates.** `opens_at`/`closes_at` are read and
   returned, never compared to `now` — `src/routes/review.routes.ts:52,56,165,394,627,755`,
   `src/ui/review/ReviewerPage.tsx:670`. They are pure display.
2. **Re-anchoring would silently shift every stored row by a day.** `fromDateInput` stores
   `Date.UTC(y,m,d)` (`EvaluationPage.tsx:45`); rendered in `America/New_York` that midnight
   is 20:00 the *previous* day. Changing the anchor without a migration corrupts every
   existing round date and task due date in place — the exact class of error the original
   contract was written to prevent.

**So: keep the encoding, restate it in the ruling's language.** Calendar-day fields
(`evaluation_rounds.opens_at/closes_at`, `speaker_tasks.due_at`, `events.starts_on/ends_on`)
are **calendar days encoded at UTC midnight**, rendered with no clock and no zone label,
identical for every reader. Update the comments at `EvaluationPage.tsx:29-33` and `:194-198`,
`ReviewerPage.tsx:252-255`, and `task-due.ts:1-12` to say *that*, so the next agent reading
"UTC" does not think it contradicts the ruling and re-open this.

The one place the calendar-day encoding still leaks into behaviour is **B3** — end-of-UTC-day
enforcement of task due dates. Fix the boundary, keep the encoding.

**This is the one item worth an operator sanity-check.** If Atin wants round dates and task
due dates re-anchored to the conference zone outright, that is a separate migration ticket,
not a line in this one.

## DST is not optional

The conference zone's offset changes. **Any implementation using a fixed offset is wrong**,
and it will pass every test written in July.

- Use `Intl.DateTimeFormat` with an explicit `timeZone` for instant → wall clock, and the
  fixed-point iteration in `AgendaPage.zonedStart:93-109` for wall clock → instant. Both are
  already in the tree, both handle DST, and both run on Workers.
- **Never** derive an offset once and reuse it.
- `zonedStart` iterates three times toward a fixed point. Two edge cases are worth an
  explicit decision and a test: a wall-clock time that **does not exist** (02:30 on a
  spring-forward morning) and one that occurs **twice** (fall-back). Pick a documented
  behaviour — settling forward on the gap and taking the first occurrence on the overlap is
  the conventional answer — and assert it rather than leaving it to whatever the loop
  happens to do.
- The design must not depend on the runtime's own zone, in either direction. Browser-local
  and Worker-local are both wrong answers; every call passes `timeZone` explicitly. (The
  Worker's own zone is UTC, which is exactly why this bug was invisible server-side — but
  nothing you write should care.)

## Where the zone gets displayed

The ruling says *"display what time zone if necessary, if relevant."* It is relevant exactly
where the reader might not be in the conference's zone and the value has a clock:

**Label it:**
- The CFP close date in the form builder (`FormsPage`) — the organizer is setting a deadline
  and may be travelling. `Close date (America/New_York)` on the field, or `EDT` beside the
  control.
- The session start on `SubmissionRecordPage` — same reason, higher stakes.
- The public form's "Closes …" (`PublicForm`) — submitters are worldwide.
- The embed CFP deadline (`EmbedPage`) — rendered on someone else's site.
- Times in outbound mail (`schedule.ts`, `merge-data.ts`) — read anywhere, days later,
  with no page around them to give context.

**Do not label it:**
- Inside the agenda builder grid, where every cell is conference-local and a repeated zone
  tag is noise. One statement of the zone in the surface's chrome is enough.
- Calendar-day values (round dates, task due dates) — no clock, no zone.
- System and audit timestamps — those are the reader's own clock by design.

Prefer the short form (`EDT`) inline and the IANA name where the surface has room. Derive it
with `Intl.DateTimeFormat(..., { timeZoneName: "short" })` rather than a hand-written map —
a hand-written map is a fixed offset wearing a disguise.

## Sequencing — display first, behaviour second

Land these as separate commits, and preferably separate PRs. They carry very different risk.

**Step 1 — the shared seam (no behaviour change).**
Extract the working pair into `src/lib/event-time.ts`: `zonedStart` from
`AgendaPage.tsx:92` and `localParts` from `track-board.tsx:124`, plus the `datetime-local`
round-trip pair built on them and a zone-label helper. Both current call sites re-import
from the new home; their behaviour is unchanged and their existing tests must stay green.
One home, so the next surface that needs this does not invent a fourth convention.

**Step 2 — display (safe, shippable alone).**
D1–D8. Nothing stored changes. This alone closes the sbek finding.

**Step 3 — behaviour (real, reviewable, riskier).**
B1, B2, B3. B1 is the most important change in this ticket. Say plainly in the PR that B2
moves when reminders fire for organizers outside the conference zone.

## Test strategy

The suite must prove correctness **from a machine whose local zone is neither UTC nor the
conference's**. That is the whole point: a test that runs in UTC cannot tell the broken
implementation from the fixed one.

- **Pin the machine zone with `process.env.TZ` in try/finally.** The established pattern is
  `tests/unit/abstract-management.MRQ-169.test.ts:243-257` and the `inNewYork` helper in the
  preserved branch's `tests/unit/forms-close-date.eval11.test.ts:14-22`. Verified working on
  this repo's Node (v26): assigning `process.env.TZ` mid-process moves both `Date` and
  `Intl`'s default zone.
- **Pin it to a third zone.** The old test pinned `America/New_York` — the same zone as the
  fixture conference — which now proves less than it should, because browser-local and
  conference-local coincide. Pin the machine to something that is *neither*, e.g.
  `Asia/Tokyo`, with a `America/New_York` conference. Then browser-local, UTC, and
  conference-local are three distinct answers and only one passes.
- **Always restore in `finally`**, and keep these tests in files whose other tests do not
  depend on the ambient zone — `process.env.TZ` is process-global and `maxConcurrency` is 8
  (`vitest.node.config.ts`).
- **DST both ways.** Round-trip wall-clock values either side of both 2027 transitions, as
  the preserved branch does; a fixed offset must fail at least one. Add the nonexistent-time
  and doubled-time cases from the DST section above.
- **Assert both halves of the read-back bug**, as the branch does: the control reads back
  `2027-04-30`, *and* the stored instant really is `2027-05-01` in UTC. That is what makes
  it legible that storage was never wrong.
- **Worker-side rendering** (`schedule.ts`, `merge-data.ts`) is tested in the worker project,
  where `process.env.TZ` does nothing. Prove those by asserting an explicit expected string
  for a fixture zone — that the mail says the conference-local time, not an ISO stamp.
- **Existing tests that must stay green, unmodified**, because they encode the calendar-day
  contract this ticket deliberately preserves: `tests/unit/task-due.MRQ-114.test.ts`,
  `tests/unit/abstract-management.MRQ-169.test.ts:242` ("reviewer round close uses the
  configured calendar day"), `tests/unit/conference-dates.MRQ-142.test.ts`,
  `tests/unit/calendar-ics.AC-95-96-97.test.ts`,
  `tests/integration/attendee-schedule.MRQ-132.test.ts`. **If one of these goes red, the
  change is wrong — do not edit the test.**
- `npm test` and `npm run pr-gate` both green. Read the `status` field, not the wall clock:
  `pass-over-budget` is a warn.

## Non-goals

- **No `Temporal`, no date library.** Zero date dependencies today; keep it that way.
- **No per-user timezone preference.** The ruling is one zone per event, full stop.
- **No storage migration.** No stored instant is rewritten by this ticket. Every stored
  value stays epoch-ms UTC; only interpretation at the edges changes.
- **No re-anchoring of calendar-day fields.** See the contract section. If the operator
  wants it, it is a separate migration ticket.
- **No touching the instant comparisons** that gate form open/close, the portal, delivery
  health, or the reminder window. They are already correct.
- **No sweeping audit/system timestamps into the conference zone.**
- **No API shape change.** `opens_at`/`closes_at`/`starts_at` stay `z.number().int()` epoch
  ms (`src/routes/forms.routes.ts:49-50,132-133`). The API is instant-based and correct.
- **No deploy, no demo reset, no `loop.sh`, no `.deploy-freeze` edit** — an eval round is
  grading a frozen build.

## Acceptance criteria

A builder can check every one of these itself.

1. `src/lib/event-time.ts` exists and is the single home for wall-clock ⇄ instant conversion
   and zone labelling. `AgendaPage` and `track-board` import from it; their existing tests
   pass unmodified.
2. **Grep proves the sweep**: no `datetime-local` control in `src/ui/` writes via
   `new Date(value).getTime()` or reads via `toISOString()`. The two are `FormsPage.tsx:493`
   and `SubmissionRecordPage.tsx:660`.
3. With the machine zone pinned to `Asia/Tokyo` and the conference in `America/New_York`,
   typing `2027-04-30 23:59` into the CFP close date and saving reads back
   `2027-04-30 23:59`, and the value written to `forms.closes_at` is
   `2027-05-01T03:59:00.000Z`.
4. Under the same pinning, placing a session at `09:00` on `SubmissionRecordPage` stores an
   instant that the agenda grid, the portal, and the ICS feed all render as `09:00`.
5. The public form, the embed CFP block, and the outbound reminder mail all state the same
   close moment as the form builder, each in the conference zone. The mail body contains no
   raw ISO 8601 stamp.
6. Every surface listed under "Label it" names the zone; no surface under "Do not label it"
   gained one.
7. `events.timezone` is read from `useEventContext().event.timezone` (or the public payload)
   at every changed site. **No changed site falls back to the browser's or the Worker's zone
   when the event is not yet loaded** — it renders the surface's existing empty placeholder.
8. `src/ui/settings/EventSettings.tsx` and `src/ui/setup/CreateConferencePage.tsx` offer the
   same timezone list from one shared constant, and a conference whose zone is outside that
   list still displays its own zone as the selected value.
9. Calendar-day fields are untouched in storage, and the comments at
   `EvaluationPage.tsx:29-33` / `:194-198`, `ReviewerPage.tsx:252-255`, and `task-due.ts:1-12`
   state the calendar-day rule in the ruling's language rather than justifying "UTC".
10. A speaker task due `2027-05-01` for a `America/New_York` conference is not overdue at
    `2027-05-01T20:00:00-04:00`, and is overdue at `2027-05-02T00:00:01-04:00`.
11. DST: wall-clock round trips hold either side of both 2027 US transitions, and the
    nonexistent-time and doubled-time cases have a documented, asserted behaviour.
12. The five named existing test files pass unmodified. `npm test` and `npm run pr-gate`
    report `pass` or `pass-over-budget`.
13. The 11-step walkthrough loop still completes with zero dead ends.

## Follow-ups — record here, do not mint a second ticket

- Re-anchoring calendar-day fields to the conference zone, with a storage migration, if the
  operator overrules the contract resolution above.
- A conference-zone clock in the shell chrome ("It is 14:20 in New York"), so an organizer
  working from elsewhere always has the conference's time in view.
- Auditing whether any of the "leave as-is" audit timestamps genuinely wants the conference
  zone, one at a time and with a reason each.
- A lint or `check:` script that fails on a `datetime-local` control whose handlers do not
  route through `src/lib/event-time.ts`, so the fourth instance of this bug cannot be
  written.
data.title: The conference timezone is the only timezone: every organizer-set time is conference-local

data.body:
Shipped in PR #254, squashed to 7068e268 on 2026-08-14; the feature branch was deleted after merge.

Implemented the conference-local event-time seam and the organizer-set/read behavior: SubmissionRecordPage session placement, CFP close writes and reminder timing, conference-local task overdue enforcement, public/embed/mail/merge displays, and the person-only comms fallback timezone path. Reviewer 323 approved the final fix at d2b6e4d9 after verifying the rendered person-only outbox body and that the inner join is lossless for eligible rows. GitHub CI fast-gate passed; the three TypeScript projects and targeted mail regression passed; the five protected test files remained unmodified.

Important shipped consequence and boundary: no stored epoch is rewritten. Existing instants can now display a different wall time or date because rendering is event-local. Historically mis-stored browser-zone values remain mis-stored and may now be displayed confidently in the conference zone. Auditing or repairing those rows is an operator-owned follow-up and is NOT covered by MRQ-201; no audit or repair was performed here. Do not infer that fixing the writer repaired historical rows.

No migration, deployment, frozen-build change, demo reset, or follow-up ticket was created.
